headline: CHINA ACTIVATES RARE EARTH EXPORT BLACKLIST JULY 1 — MP MATERIALS AND USA RARE EARTH HIT; MOFCOM ENFORCEMENT LIVE
snippet: China's MOFCOM published Announcement No. 26 of 2026 on June 24, activating formal enforcement procedures for strategic mineral and rare earth dual-use export controls effective July 1, 2026 — the same day China added 10 U.S. entities to its export control blacklist, including rare earth miners MP Materials and USA Rare Earth. The escalation follows a sixfold rise in neodymium-praseodymium oxide prices since January and a tripling of tungsten concentrate prices, codifying Beijing's leverage over Western supply chains into an active enforcement regime for the first time.

headline: "WHEN WILL THE BLEEDING STOP?" — SILVER'S 7-WEEK LOSING STREAK, GOLD -2% LAST WEEK; ALL EYES ON THURSDAY PAYROLLS
snippet: Gold fell more than 2% last week and silver extended its losing streak to seven consecutive weeks as persistent U.S. dollar strength and Fed hawkishness continue to outweigh structural supply-deficit fundamentals — with precious metals approaching significant technical support zones while Asian physical buyers absorb paper-market liquidation near US$4,000 gold and US$57 silver. Thursday's June Non-Farm Payrolls report is now the market's most likely short-term circuit breaker: a soft number would reduce September rate-hike probability and could end the selling wave that has dominated precious metals since late January.

headline: STAR COPPER ACQUIRES TWO DRILL-READY BC COPPER PORPHYRIES FROM EASTFIELD — ZYMO AND INDATA ADD 87-HOLE HISTORY (CSE:STCU)
source_name: Investing News Network / Star Copper Corp.
snippet: Star Copper Corp. (CSE:STCU) agreed June 30, 2026 to acquire 100% of Eastfield Resources' Zymo Copper-Gold Project (18,184 ha, near Smithers, BC) and a 95.3% stake in the Indata Copper-Gold-Molybdenum Project (near Fort St. James, BC), paying 10 million shares — Indata alone has 87 historical drill holes totalling more than 10,000 metres across a porphyry-copper system permitted through 2030. The deal gives Star Copper three significant BC copper projects at a time when the COMEX-LME tariff arbitrage from the U.S. Section 232 copper report is drawing fresh institutional attention to North American copper assets.

headline: 63.88 g/t GOLD AT SURFACE: LATIN METALS CONFIRMS HIGH-GRADE VEIN AT LA FLORA, ARGENTINA — Q3 DRILL COMING (TSXV:LMS)
snippet: Latin Metals Inc. (TSXV:LMS) reported June 29, 2026 surface sampling results from the La Flora Project in Santa Cruz Province, Argentina, returning up to 63.88 g/t gold and 175.34 g/t silver within a one-kilometre-long high-grade epithermal vein system confirmed by exploration partner Daura Gold Corp. The results validate La Flora as a priority drill target in the prolific southern Patagonia epithermal belt; Daura's Phase II drill program targeting both Cerro Bayo and La Flora is planned for Q3 2026.

headline: BRIEN LUNDIN: GOLD AND SILVER MINERS SHOWING "RARE GENERATIONAL OPPORTUNITY" — FUNDAMENTALS INTACT, PRICE DISAGREES
snippet: Gold Newsletter editor Brien Lundin argues that the current correction in gold and silver mining equities has opened a valuation gap that project-level fundamentals do not support: producers are generating record free cash flow at US$4,000 gold, developer NAV multiples have collapsed to multi-year lows, and central bank gold buying and industrial silver demand from solar and AI infrastructure remain structurally robust — conditions historically associated with the highest-return entry windows of the secular precious metals cycle. Lundin specifically identifies the late-June to mid-July period as the critical accumulation window for investors with a 12-month horizon.

headline: VIRGINIA SAVES PRECIOUS METALS TAX EXEMPTION HOURS BEFORE MIDNIGHT EXPIRY — GOLD AND SILVER PURCHASES TAX-FREE THROUGH 2028
snippet: Virginia signed HB 30 on June 30, 2026 — just hours before midnight — extending the state's sales tax exemption on gold, silver, and platinum bullion and legal tender coins through 2028, after the Sound Money Defense League and Money Metals Exchange mobilised thousands of in-state grassroots investors to pressure key legislators ahead of the June 30 sunset deadline. Without the extension, Virginia would have reimposed sales taxes on precious metals purchases for the first time since 2013, joining a shrinking minority of U.S. states that tax bullion.

headline: BOLIVIA DUMPS 15-YEAR DOLLAR PEG, BOLIVIANO DOWN 40% — SILVER AND LITHIUM OPERATORS FACE SOUTH AMERICAN COST SHOCK
snippet: Bolivia abandoned its 15-year fixed exchange rate of 6.96 bolivianos per U.S. dollar on June 26, 2026, replacing it with a freely floating regime that immediately pushed the rate to approximately 9.73 bolivianos per dollar — an implied 40% devaluation — as the central bank's dollar reserves fell to critically low levels. Bolivia is one of the world's largest lithium resource holders and a meaningful silver producer; the currency collapse raises dollar-denominated production costs for domestic operators, complicates royalty and offtake structures, and adds sovereign risk to projects seeking international project financing.

headline: S&P GLOBAL: ELEVATED COPPER PRICES "OVEREXTENDED" — ANALYSTS SAY CORRECTION HAS FURTHER TO RUN NEAR $6/LB COMEX
snippet: S&P Global Market Intelligence analysts published July 1, 2026 that the prolonged period of elevated copper prices has become "overextended," with COMEX copper hovering below US$6/lb near its lowest level in seven weeks as demand-side uncertainty — slowing China property activity, U.S. rate-hike risk, and inventory correction after tariff-driven COMEX pre-positioning — weighs on the near-term price. The analysis identifies simultaneous mine supply disruptions at Grasberg (mudslide), Kamoa (acid plant), and Chilean operations as the primary buffer preventing a sharper correction into H2 2026.

headline: INN Q2 URANIUM REVIEW: SPOT HOLDS $84-87/LB AFTER $101 PEAK — KAZATOMPROM QUOTA CUT RESHAPES SUPPLY PICTURE
snippet: The uranium spot price consolidated in a US$84–$87 per pound range through Q2 2026 after touching US$101 in January — a 16% pullback that analysts characterise as technical rather than structural, as Kazatomprom's mid-year quota reduction from 85 million to 77 million pounds removes near-term supply without altering the long-term deficit picture for 2028–2032. INN's Q2 review notes that the Northshore Global Uranium Mining Index gained 17% in June while utility term contracting volumes are finally accelerating after years of under-contracting, with the Sprott Physical Uranium Trust NAV returning to a premium for the first time in eight months.

headline: CSIS: CHINA'S RARE EARTH RESTRICTIONS ONE YEAR ON — WESTERN SUPPLY CHAINS STILL FRAGILE, SUBSTITUTION MOVING SLOWLY
snippet: A Center for Strategic and International Studies analysis marking approximately one year since China's initial rare earth export restriction campaign finds that while Western governments have dramatically accelerated policy and funding responses, actual non-Chinese processing capacity remains nascent and structural dependence on Chinese rare earth refining has barely shifted — with new U.S., Australian, and Canadian projects needing an estimated 3–5 more years before meaningful production arrives. The CSIS report frames July 1's activation of MOFCOM's new enforcement procedures as an escalation from informal pressure to formal legal mechanism, arguing that the window for orderly Western supply chain diversification is narrowing.
